subject: Insurance
title: Roman Burial Clubs
description: A fast breakdown of Roman Burial Clubs for builders.

hook.text: Roman soldiers formed 'collegia' that paid funeral costs when a member died. Monthly dues funded the payouts.

buildup.text: A proper Roman burial was expensive. Without one, families faced shame. The clubs guaranteed dignity in death.

discovery.text: These clubs also paid survivors a benefit. They were the first life insurance—centuries before the term existed.

twist.text: The Roman government tried to ban the clubs, fearing they'd become political groups. Insurance met regulation early.

climax.text: Burial clubs survived bans because the need was too strong. People will always organize against uncertainty.

punchline.text: Monthly dues, funeral guaranteed. Rome invented life insurance.
